questions.qtext: What's the number of 3-digit natural numbers, in which digits are in non-decreasing order?
questions.solution:
Answer: 8

Source solution 1 (score: 3)

Answer 165

  • By using IODB Template ,stars bars concept.
  • We required 3 digits so stars will be 3.
  • Since, non decreasing the boxes will contain {1,2,..9}. So 8 bars.
  • Boxes won't have zero, because if 0 is selected firstly it cannot be n digit and secondly later on other digits we cannot select 0 because of non decreasing order of the digits( should be increasing order)
  • Finally we will be having 3 stars and 8 bars
  • Answer is 8+3 C 3.

questions.qtext: $m$ identical balls are to be placed in $n$ distinct bags. You are given that $m \geq kn$, where $k$ is a natural number $\geq 1$. In how many ways can the balls be placed in the bags if each bag must contain at least $k$ balls?

options.text: $\left( \begin{array}{c} m - kn + n + k - 2 \\ n - k \end{array} \right)$

questions.solution:
Answer: B

Source solution 1 (score: 2)

Detailed Video Solution with Complete Analysis:

Question Source: https://gateoverflow.in/924/gate-cse-2003-question-34?show=469200#c469200

Source solution 2 (score: 0)
Answer option B



Clearly it the case of IODB(IDENTICAL OBJECTS AND DISTINGUISHABLE BOXES) Template.

We can use star - bars concept.

⚫ m stars and m-kn is because of every bag should have atleast k balls of total n bags.

⚫n bags so n-1 Bars.

Therefore by using stars and bars concept the answer is m-kn+n-1 C n-1.
